jobs.description: EDGE Student Internships & Co-op Programs | Rockwell Automation | US Loading Careers Internship & Co-op Opportunities for Students Hands-on projects. An unforgettable experience. View Open Student Roles Careers Teams & People Student & Early Careers Students & Early Career Programs Students & Early Career Programs Student Internships & Co-op Programs Student Internships & Co-op Programs Early Career Programs Early Career Programs Supply Chain Careers Employee Spotlight Veterans View Jobs Want to make an impact? You’ve come to the right place. A professional internship or co-op at Rockwell Automation can launch you on a rewarding career path, helping make the world more productive and sustainable. At Rockwell Automation, we connect the imaginations of people with the potential of technology to expand what is humanly possible. As an intern or co-op you’ll contribute to our mission, immersing yourself in strategic projects while building a global network and becoming a valuable part of our team. As an EDGE participant, you’ll have opportunities to Expand, Discover, Grow and Excel in ways that will set you apart and set you up for career success. Connect With Us Follow our Careers pages on social media to stay up to date on announcements, awards, our company culture, and what makes Rockwell a great place to work – in other words, all things #LifeatROK. EDGE Student Programs Learn and grow while making a real-world impact. We offer many different internship and co-op placements, including summer internships, semester-long co-ops, and full and part-time internships globally. A variety of programs are available, spanning educational levels and locations across the globe. While the typical recruiting periods for these positions are during Spring and Fall in the U.S., they vary by region and country, so we encourage you to check our listings regularly. Internship and Co-Op Programs Engineering Computer Science Technology Supply Chain Business Functions Educational Levels High School/Secondary School Undergraduate/Post-secondary Advanced Degrees (MBA, Master’s) Typical Hiring Locations U.S. Poland Mexico Canada Brazil China France Germany Spain Colombia Dominican Republic India Australia Why Intern at Rockwell Automation? Be Part of Something BIG As a global leader in industrial automation and digital transformation, we employ nearly 23,000 problem solvers in more than 100 countries. As an intern or co-op you’ll launch your career by being a valued part of our global team. Build A Global Network From virtual meet ups to in-person events, you’ll have continuous opportunities to make new connections, form life-long friendships, and build a strong network of professionals you can turn to for guidance and career advice. Contribute Every Day Our interns work alongside industry professionals - many former interns and co-ops themselves - to help solve real-world problems, support our customers, and work on business-critical projects. Your colleagues are dedicated to helping you apply what you’re learning in school while you gain critical industry experience and insights. Give Your Future An EDGE Landing a professional internship or co-op at Rockwell Automation is just the beginning. While you’re here, you’ll have the chance to learn about future career paths and early career programs so you can hit the ground running after you graduate. Eligibility Guidelines Requirements to be considered for an internship or co-op are as follows. To be considered for a high school/secondary school internship, you must be actively enrolled as a student. To be considered for a university internship (Bachelor’s, Master’s, MBA), you must be actively enrolled as a full-time student, pursuing a degree relevant to the role to which you apply and plan to return to school for at least one term after the completion of your internship. To be considered for a university co-op (U.S. and Canada), you must be actively enrolled as a full-time student, registered with and meet the requirements of your university’s co-op program, pursuing a degree relevant to the role to which you apply, and plan to return to school for at least one term after the completion of your co-op. Other eligibility requirements vary by position and location. Please reference individual job postings for specific requirements. Recommended For You Loading Ready to get started? Our rotational and training early career programs are designed to give new university graduates as well as graduates with a year or two of professional experience a unique, immersive experience that will prepare you for long-term career success. As an EDGE participant, the opportunities to Expand, Discover, Grow and Excel will set you apart and help cultivate an amazing career. Connect With Us Follow our Careers pages on social media to stay up to date on announcements, awards, our company culture, and what makes Rockwell a great place to work – in other words, all things #LifeatROK. EDGE Early Career Programs Rotational Programs Establish a strong professional foundation Do you embrace the unfamiliar? Crave new experiences? Our rotational programs just might be your career dream come true, expanding your possibilities through a powerful combination of robust work assignments, targeted training, and meaningful development opportunities. You’ll build a global professional network and deepen your understanding of our operating segments and functional teams, all while contributing to high-impact projects throughout the company and building a strong foundation for future professional success. Training Programs Practical experience, tools and support to strengthen your skills Our training programs are designed to empower new and recent graduates with the tools, knowledge, and support they need to deliver great outcomes for our customers. Each training program is a unique blend of several (or all) of the following: classroom learning, lab work, field assignments, project-based learning and professional development. Our training programs are designed to help you establish the fundamental skills you’ll need to succeed on your chosen career path, create a sense of community, and expand your network. Completing a training program will help reduce the time it takes for you to be effective in your chosen role, and strengthen your ability to use Rockwell Automation resources to solve problems. Training programs vary in duration, depending on the program. Discover Your Career Path Our EDGE programs offer an environment that will prepare you as a leader of change in a variety of areas depending on your interests, strengths and ideal career path. jobs.title: View our Talent Acquisition Privacy Statement
jobs.description: Talent Acquisition Privacy Statement | Rockwell Automation | US Loading Talent Acquisition Privacy Statement Scope Rockwell Automation takes the privacy and protection of your personal data seriously. With this Privacy Statement Rockwell Automation wishes to explain to you how it collects, uses, shares and protects personal data that you may provide through its recruitment systems and/or that it may otherwise collect during its selection and recruitment processes. We encourage you to read this Privacy Statement before submitting information. The term “Rockwell Automation” or “the Company” as used in this Privacy Statement refers to Rockwell Automation, Inc. and its subsidiaries and divisions that you interact with and that use the global, regional and/or local recruitment systems operated by or on behalf of Rockwell Automation. If you are a California resident, you may have additional privacy rights. Please see the section “Supplemental California Talent Acquisition Privacy Notice” at the end of this Privacy Statement. Personal Data Collection Rockwell Automation uses a number of selection and recruitment systems to communicate job opportunities that become available within Rockwell Automation and to receive and process job seekers’ inquiries and job applications. You are free to use the systems to explore and apply for such opportunities. For this purpose, the systems facilitate the submission of your contact details and your personal data normally required in order to evaluate your suitability for a job, such as your interests, your curriculum vitae and details of your educational qualifications, experiences and skills. Rockwell Automation may also receive such personal data from talent acquisition and recruitment service providers. It may also collect personal data about you from industry and career networking events and platforms and/or from professional networking sites. During its selection and recruitment process, Rockwell Automation will collect additional information about you, such as through interviews, reference checking, and/or possible skills and behavioral assessments. Rockwell Automation runs a Referral Program whereby our employees are encouraged to propose possible candidates for open jobs. As part of this Referral Program, personal data about you will be provided to Rockwell Automation. Our employees are encouraged to obtain your prior consent for such referrals. The Company is committed to the reliability and competence of its employees. Therefore, in the final phase of the recruitment process a third party may be engaged to perform a pre-employment screening (background check). You will be informed about the scope, and will be requested to provide specific permission to complete these background check activities. For executive or technical positions, Rockwell Automation or third parties engaged by Rockwell Automation may run additional checks and verifications related to your skills and qualifications, as well as behavioral assessments. Personal data collected and processed during the selection and recruitment process may vary by country and the nature of the role for which you are being considered. For example, the Company may ask USA and Canada residents to complete a virtual, self-scheduled video interview session and to submit the recording to Rockwell Automation. You may also be invited to use AI assistants and chat bots for automated back-and-forth interview scheduling and communication. In general, you are free to submit any or all of the requested information. However, when you register on one or more of the systems, you may need to complete required fields pertaining to your name, contact information, and employment and/or educational history, as well as to choose a username and password. Some fields are required, and some are optional. The fields that require you to complete information requested are denoted with a star. If you choose to withhold any personal data for required fields, it may not be possible for you to gain access to certain parts of the systems and/or to apply for job opportunities. Use of Personal Data and Legal Basis Rockwell Automation uses your personal data to evaluate your suitability for one or more jobs, to identify the most suitable candidates for these jobs, to consider alternative job opportunities for you and for related purposes up to and including making job offers. The legal basis for collecting and processing your personal data are: Rockwell Automation legitimate business interests to find the right job seekers for its job offers, to select the best, suitable candidates and to demonstrate that proper recruitment processes are followed (for example in the event of a complaint; for example, to monitor equal opportunity policies), Your consent, and, Where applicable, requirements to comply with reporting and other legal obligations. Rockwell Automation will not use your personal data for decision-making based solely on automated processing, if the decision produces legal effects concerning you or significantly affects you, unless you give your explicit, prior consent. When Rockwell Automation applies automated decision-making with your consent, you can request an explanation about the automated decision-making using your personal information and you can request that a natural person reviews the decision where it was exclusively based on automated processing. Processing of Sensitive Personal Data On an exceptional basis, Rockwell Automation may request certain sensitive personal data, such as gender, race, ethnicity, nationality, and citizenship as well as medical data. It is optional for job candidates to provide this information, unless and to the extent that the collection and processing of such sensitive personal data is required by law or generally accepted standards and practices or is necessary for Rockwell Automation to comply with its obligations or to exercise certain rights in the field of employment and social securi

jobs.title: Privacy Policy
jobs.description: Privacy and Cookies Policy | Rockwell Automation | US Loading Privacy and Cookies Policy What We Do at Rockwell Automation Rockwell Automation Inc. and its subsidiaries (collectively “we” or ”Rockwell Automation”), are global leaders in digital transformation and industrial automation. We provide market leading hardware, software, services, and solutions that help our customers and their people be more productive and sustainable. Statement of Purpose We respect your privacy. We are committed to protecting it. We believe that responsible handling of data—all data, not just personal data—is integral to our mission and growing more important as our world becomes more connected and individuals realize the advancements that data can enable. This Privacy and Cookies Policy (the “Policy”) is part of our commitment to responsible data handling. The Policy explains the types of personal data we may collect and how we may use, share, store, and secure that personal data. For purposes of this Policy, “personal data” means information (either on its own or in combination with other information) that identifies you, allows you to be identified , or could be linked to your household (collectively, “you” or the “User”). This includes information such as: your name; your physical address; your email address or other business contact details; your online identifiers like your IP address; the details of your use of products and services; and any other information that becomes personally associated with you. This Policy applies to all of the personal data you may provide to us or that we may access through our websites (the “Sites” or a “Site”); through any of our online applications, platforms, channels, products, or services (collectively, “Products and Services”); or through our business interactions. This policy applies where Rockwell Automation is acting as controller. To the extent we may process your personal data as a processor on behalf of the company you are employed by or are otherwise associated with, this Policy will not apply and we may enter into a separate data processing agreement with your company. Rockwell Automation Communications Preference Center You can configure how you would like Rockwell Automation to communicate with you at any time. To change your preferences, please visit our Communications Preference Center . Collection of Personal Data When do we collect personal data? We collect personal data in the following situations: When you visit or use one of our Sites; When you purchase or use one of our Products and Services; When you voluntarily provide your personal data to us (for example, when you opted-in to receive marketing emails, when you registered for an account on a Site or in connection with Products and Services, or when you completed a web form to register for an event) ; When the company or organization you work with provides it to us; When you participate in webinars, seminars, trade fairs, or other events; When you visit our social media pages; When you or others share information publicly (for example, by posting publicly on LinkedIn or publishing material to corporate websites); When you visit our offices; When you receive communications from us, including emails, phone calls, or text messages; When you use our Products and Services, including customer-care and technical support for those Products and Services; When it is necessary for us to provide Products and Services or otherwise do business with you or the company or organization you work with; When we buy services from selected third-party vendors that utilize aggregated cookies or similar data to target ads based on common characteristics; and/or At other times when we have disclosed the collection and intended use to you in advance through this Policy or at the time of collection. You are not required to provide personal data to us in these situations. However, if you do not, we may not be able to provide certain services or information you may request. What types of personal data do we collect? We collect these types of personal data: Type of Personal Data Additional Information Relevant business contact information This includes information such as your name, the name of the company or organization you work for, your business address, your location of operation, your title, your email address, and your telephone number. Personal contact, preferences, demographic, and interest information You might give us this information when registering for events such as webinars, seminars, and trade fairs. Information that your web browser automatically makes available to us whenever you visit a Site This information is obtained through commonly used tracking technologies, such as cookies and web beacons, and may include: Your Internet Protocol (IP) address; How you navigated to the Site; The domain name of the last website you visited; The number of times you visited the Site; The pages you’ve viewed on the Site; Links you’ve clicked, comments you’ve made, or your likes and shares; Your browser’s type, version, and language; and/or The date and time of your query. There is more information about cookies and our use of them below. Usage data such as log files showing how you interact with our Products and Services This information includes log data showing the activities of individuals using our software and platform products (for example, FactoryTalk Production Center, Fiix’s CMMS, and the Plex platform). The information may also include information about your interactions with customer-care and technical support, such as your communications and the contents of them, which may be reviewed and analyzed by our employees, contractors, and/or third-party vendors (possibly with the assistance of analytics technologies). We use this information to optimize plant operations and improve the functioning of our smart, digital manufacturing options.
